title: Normalize the derived tensor adjunction for a fixed coefficient calculus
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l and a scheme W on which l is invertible. Let S be a coefficient derived system calculus with its coherence [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and let M be any OrdinaryModel [def-trf-completion-unit-models]. Suppose c identifies the termwise limit functor with roosLimitFunctor, with every degreewise projection equal to the corresponding ordinary limit projection. Let eta be a right-derived unit for the fixed coefficientConstantTowerLimit, normalized on every K-injective tower J by eta_J followed by rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso_J equal to Q(c_J inverse). Define systemLimitUnit as Q(M.limitComparison), followed by eta after tower restriction, followed by coefficientConstantTowerLimit applied to the inverse exact-restriction localization factor. This composite is invertible on every K-injective system. There exists a universal left-derived comparison epsilon from Q followed by S.reduction to M.quotient followed by Q, invertible on every flat-term K-flat complex. Its finite evaluation is S.reductionEvaluation followed by the fixed coefficientFiniteReductionModel, including the ordinary M.evaluation and exact-evaluation localization factors. For every chain map a from M.quotient(Q) to I, its transpose under S.adjunction after epsilon equals Q of the ordinary chain transpose followed by systemLimitUnit_I. No ordinary-model existence, tower-unit existence or Roos isomorphism is asserted.

proof.text: Apply restricted_limit_acyclic to a K-injective tower resolution of the restriction of a K-injective system I. The given eta normalization makes eta invertible on the resolution. Naturality and cancellation of the images of the two quasi-isomorphisms make eta invertible at the restricted tower, so the displayed composite systemLimitUnit is invertible at I. The K-injective derivability structure then makes this composite a universal right-derived comparison.

Use finite scalar extension preservation of quasi-isomorphisms on K-flat complexes, M.evaluation, exact evaluation localization factors, and S.isIso_iff_evaluations to prove that M.tensor inverts such quasi-isomorphisms. Flat-term K-flat resolutions form a resolving class in the homotopy category. Construct its universal left-derived functor with leftDerived_from_resolvingClass and use derivedAdjunctionOfResolvingClass with the composite right comparison. This gives the normalized Hom equation for every chain map, not just resolutions.

Compare the new left adjoint and S.reduction via Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq. Precompose the left comparison by this isomorphism. Its unit-compatibility equation transports the chain-map Hom equation to S.adjunction; the Kan-extension transport lemma preserves universality, and compositions of isomorphisms preserve K-flat computation.

Specialize the transported Hom equation to the identity of M.quotient(Q) to obtain its normalized unit equation. Apply finiteComparison_of_unit to that equation. Combine this finite equality with the already constructed universal comparison, its K-flat computation, the full Hom equation, and the K-injective system computation.

theorem derivedAdjunctionComparison_exists
    [∀ x : W, Invertible (l : W.residueField x)]
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E W)
    (_coherence : CoefficientDerivedSystemCoherence l E W S)
    (M : OrdinaryModel l E W)
    (c : (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E W) ⥤
      scalarReductionSource l E W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ≅ roosLimitFunctor)
    (_hc : ∀ (Z : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E W) ℤ)
      (n : ℕ) (p : ℤ),
      (c.hom.app Z ≫ limit.π Z.asFunctor (op n)).f p = limit.π (Z.X p) (op n))
    (η : roosLimitFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ coefficientConstantTowerLimit l E W)
    (_hηnorm : ∀ (J : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E W) ℤ)
      [J.IsKInjective], η.app J ≫
        ((lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E W) ⥤
          scalarReductionSource l E W).rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso J).hom =
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (c.inv.app J))
    (_hη : (coefficientConstantTowerLimit l E W).IsRightDerivedFunctor η
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E W) (.up ℤ))) :
    (∀ (I : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E W) ℤ),
      I.IsKInjective → IsIso ((systemLimitUnit l E W M η).app I)) ∧
    ∃ (ε : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ S.reduction ⟶ M.quotient l E W ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q),
      S.reduction.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (scalarReductionSource l E W) (.up ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ (Q : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E W) ℤ),
        Q.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients → (∀ p : ℤ, (Q.X p).IsFlatOnSite) →
          IsIso (ε.app Q)) ∧
      (∀ (Q : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E W) ℤ)
        (hQ : Q.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients)
        (_hflat : ∀ p : ℤ, (Q.X p).IsFlatOnSite) (n : ℕ),
        (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E W n).map (ε.app Q) ≫
            (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E W n).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
              ((M.quotient l E W).obj Q) ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map
              ((NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex (M.evaluation n) (.up ℤ)).hom.app Q) =
          (S.reductionEvaluation n).hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q) ≫
            (coefficientFiniteReductionModel l E W Q hQ n).hom) ∧
      (∀ (Q : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E W) ℤ)
        (I : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E W) ℤ)
        (a : (M.quotient l E W).obj Q ⟶ I),
        S.adjunction.homEquiv (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I)
            (ε.app Q ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map a) =
          DerivedCategory.Q.map
              ((M.adjunction.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).homEquiv Q I a) ≫
            (systemLimitUnit l E W M η).app I)
